table_clearance_plan.safety: clearance moves are dry-run by default and reject deltas larger than --max-delta-deg
table_clearance_plan.lesson: From home to table clearance, move shoulder_front and shoulder_side first so the wrist does not sweep the table.

left_arm_v2_1.reason: In v2 clearance, shoulder_front and elbow were stable but not linked; shoulder_front finished before elbow moved, so the arm path did not match the intended table-clearance trajectory.
left_arm_v2_1.change: v2.1 keeps v2's three-layer active/strong-hold/base-hold control, but couples shoulder_front and elbow during clearance when both are target joints. They move together in one group interpolation and elbow is skipped later instead of moving a second time.

failed_initial_test.observation: Coupling worked, but full-force simultaneous shoulder_front/elbow motion shook. v2 sequential clearance remained stable.

flexible_coupling_update.reason: The simultaneous large shoulder_front and elbow movement needs lower proportional gain and more damping than single-joint clearance.
flexible_coupling_update.extra_hold: During coupled shoulder_front/elbow motion, shoulder_side is promoted from base hold to strong clearance hold.
flexible_coupling_update.escape_hatch: Use --no-coupled-shoulder-elbow to disable v2.1 coupling and run v2-style sequential clearance.

flexible_coupling_test.observation: Large shaking was greatly improved, but a brief light shake appeared during the motion and quickly disappeared.

continuous_coupling_update.reason: The remaining brief shake is likely caused by 5-degree segment boundaries during the coupled shoulder_front/elbow group motion.
continuous_coupling_update.change: The coupled shoulder_front/elbow phase now keeps the same total duration but removes internal step boundaries by running one continuous interpolation. Later clearance joints still use --step-deg segmentation.

home_shake_after_coupling_update.observation: Home shook after clearance; shoulder_rotate was commanded for only about 0.7 deg with high active gain and ended with high tau.
home_shake_after_coupling_update.fix: v2.1 home now uses a 2.0 deg joint-specific deadband for shoulder_rotate and lowers shoulder_rotate HOME_HOLD_GAINS to kp=24.0 kd=4.0.

continuous_coupling_test_after_home_fix.observation: Home no longer shakes. Clearance has only a slight transient that quickly disappears.

clearance_shoulder_rotate_deadband_updat.reason: Clearance still actively corrected shoulder_rotate by only about 0.8 deg with kp=70, which may cause a small transient similar to the previous home issue.
clearance_shoulder_rotate_deadband_updat.fix: v2.1 clearance now uses a 2.0 deg joint-specific deadband for shoulder_rotate, so it remains held instead of actively corrected for sub-2-degree error.

continuous_coupling_test_after_clearance.observation: shoulder_rotate was skipped correctly, but clearance still showed shaking during the coupled shoulder_front/elbow path.

coupled_gain_duration_update.reason: The coupled shoulder_front/elbow phase still needs softer active gains and should not spend the full computed 120 seconds in the high-load coupled trajectory.

verified_baseline.observation: Both clearance and home ran without shaking. v2.1 continuous soft coupled shoulder_front/elbow clearance is the current recommended baseline.

left_arm_v2_2.reason: User wants table clearance to link shoulder_front, shoulder_side, and elbow together instead of only shoulder_front plus elbow.
left_arm_v2_2.change: v2.2 is copied from the stable v2.1 baseline, then changes the clearance coupled group to shoulder_front, shoulder_side, and elbow. The three joints move together in one continuous interpolation when all three are targets.
left_arm_v2_2.escape_hatch: Use --no-coupled-shoulder-group to disable v2.2 three-joint coupling and use sequential behavior.

verified_test.observation: shoulder_front, shoulder_side, and elbow moved together as a coupled group. Only a very small shake appeared and quickly disappeared.

home_failed_after_three_joint_clearance.observation: After three-joint coupled clearance, home shook badly. arm_roll and shoulder_rotate showed high transient torque, indicating the old home order moved wrist/roll before retracting the large-load shoulder/elbow group.
home_failed_after_three_joint_clearance.fix: v2.2 home now defaults to elbow, shoulder_front, shoulder_side first, then shoulder_rotate, wrist, wrist_side, arm_roll. It also couples elbow+shoulder_front+shoulder_side back to home before moving wrist/roll.

verified_clearance_home_pair.observation: Three-joint coupled clearance followed by three-joint coupled home completed without shaking.

left_arm_v2_3.reason: After v2.2, user wants table clearance to keep linked motion but avoid the shaking seen when arm_roll, wrist_side, and wrist start together after the shoulder group.
left_arm_v2_3.change: v2.3 is copied from the stable v2.2 baseline. Clearance changes only the v2.2 shoulder group from shoulder_front+shoulder_side+elbow to shoulder_front+shoulder_side+elbow+arm_roll. All later joints, including wrist_side and wrist, keep v2.2 sequential behavior.
execution_order: default clearance phase 1: shoulder_front, shoulder_side, elbow, arm_roll coupled
remaining clearance joints keep v2.2 sequential behavior with holds

first_orin_test.observation: Restart reduced velocities and torques after Ctrl+C. arm_roll was only about 2.2 deg from home but still shook when actively corrected.

post_first_test_update.fix: Keep the coupled wrist group, but reduce its gains, increase damping, allow up to 80 seconds, add a 2 second preload hold before it starts, and make enable() idempotent so the second coupled phase does not re-enable all motors. arm_roll home gains were softened to kp=32 kd=4 seconds=8, and arm_roll uses a 3 deg home deadband to avoid small active corrections after interrupted clearance.
post_first_test_update.enable_behavior: Within one command, enable() now skips motors that are already enabled to avoid a second enable/mode transition at the wrist-group handoff.

second_orin_test.observation: enable() was idempotent and printed enable skip for the second coupled phase, so repeated enable was not the root cause. The wrist group still shook badly once arm_roll+wrist_side+wrist motion began.
second_orin_test.fix: After the shoulder/elbow coupled phase, v2.3 now reads the actual reached shoulder_front/shoulder_side/elbow positions and uses those reached positions as hold targets for the wrist group. During the wrist group, shoulder_front/shoulder_side/elbow use low base hold gains instead of strong clearance hold gains, reducing the chance that the wrist phase keeps forcing shoulder/elbow toward unreachable theoretical targets.

third_orin_test.observation: Using actual reached shoulder/elbow positions and low base hold gains still did not remove shaking. Home after interruption was stable when arm_roll was skipped by the 3 deg deadband, and restart was successful.
third_orin_test.fix: Change clearance logic on top of the v2.2 clearance idea: arm_roll now moves with shoulder_front+shoulder_side+elbow in the first coupled phase. No wrist coupling remains; wrist_side and wrist keep v2.2 sequential behavior.

four_joint_initial_test.observation: Direct four-joint coupled motion shook immediately when arm_roll started at the same time as shoulder_front, shoulder_side, and elbow.
four_joint_initial_test.fix: Keep arm_roll in the first coupled phase, but delay arm_roll motion until 65% of the phase progress and soften arm_roll coupled gains to kp=18 kd=6.

delayed_four_joint_clearance_test.observation: Delayed arm_roll in the first coupled clearance phase completed without shaking. wrist_side and wrist then moved sequentially with v2.2 behavior.
delayed_four_joint_clearance_test.fix: Home now also couples arm_roll with elbow+shoulder_front+shoulder_side, using kp=18 kd=6 and the same delayed arm_roll progress window [0.65, 1.0]. This should prevent the final single arm_roll home move that shook.

verified_delayed_four_joint_clearance_ho.observation: Clearance and home both completed without shaking. Clearance uses delayed shoulder_front+shoulder_side+elbow+arm_roll coupling, then wrist_side and wrist sequentially. Home uses delayed elbow+shoulder_front+shoulder_side+arm_roll coupling, then wrist and wrist_side sequentially.

shake_recovery_command.behavior: Reads status, disables selected motors, waits briefly, re-enables them, then holds the current positions with low gains before printing status again.
shake_recovery_command.safety: restart is dry-run by default; add --execute only after interrupting the shaking motion.

left_arm_v2_3.escape_hatch: Use --no-coupled-shoulder-group to disable the shoulder/elbow/arm_roll group and use v2.2-style sequential clearance.

table_clearance_controller_update.reason: Segmented clearance previously restarted each small move, causing shoulder_front to sag at every segment start and accumulate angle error.
table_clearance_controller_update.fix: clearance --step-deg now runs each joint as a continuous segmented trajectory and holds previously reached clearance joints during later joint moves.
table_clearance_controller_update.parallel_fix: clearance --parallel moves selected joints together on one continuous trajectory; use for coupled moves such as shoulder_front plus elbow.

home_controller_update.reason: Returning from table clearance caused shaking because skipped or not-yet-active joints such as shoulder_rotate were not held while large elbow/shoulder_front moves ran.
home_controller_update.fix: home now separates active movement gains, strong hold gains, and low baseline hold gains. Active joints use HOME_GAINS; coupled/completed joints use HOME_HOLD_GAINS; all other non-active joints remain enabled with HOME_BASE_HOLD_GAINS at current position.

failed_before_fix.observation: clearance was stable, but home shook because skipped joints were still enabled and held with the original HOME_GAINS.

verified_after_fix.observation: Home from table clearance no longer shakes with active/strong-hold/base-hold split.

table_clearance_hold_update.reason: During clearance, shoulder_front movement let elbow move freely because non-active joints were held with the same softer gains used for ordinary home/nudge motion.
table_clearance_hold_update.fix: clearance now separates active movement gains, strong hold gains, and low baseline hold gains. Active movement keeps the stronger gains that held elbow during shoulder_front motion; critical coupled joints and completed clearance joints use strong hold; all other non-active joints still remain enabled with low baseline hold at their current positions. Home keeps the original HOME_GAINS.

verified_test.observation: Elbow held position while shoulder_front moved.

failed_full_clearance_before_split.observation: Elbow held during shoulder_front motion, but full-arm clearance began shaking after later joints because all non-active joints were held for a long time with the stronger clearance gains.

failed_full_clearance_with_all_joints_en.observation: Even after splitting move and hold gains, full-arm clearance shook immediately when all ordered joints were enabled at startup. Sequential clearance should only enable the active joint plus the minimum required hold joints.
failed_full_clearance_with_all_joints_en.fix: Sequential clearance no longer enables all joints at startup. For each step it enables only the active joint and clearance_hold_targets_for(active).

rejected_minimal_hold_approach.reason: Keeping only the active joint and a small strong-hold set enabled leaves unrelated joints physically loose, which is unsafe for the full arm.
rejected_minimal_hold_approach.replacement: All non-active joints are now held. Critical/completed joints use strong hold gains; unrelated joints use low baseline hold at current position.

verified_full_clearance_after_fix.observation: Full-arm clearance no longer shakes, and all non-active joints remain held.

confirmed_safe_over_table.note: table clearance v2 confirmed safe over table

notes: Shoulder_front did not reach final clearance target in one staged run and showed high transient torque.
User visually confirmed the arm could hold this short transition posture.
Elbow large move was split into 5 degree steps.
After elbow moved, shoulder_front torque dropped from about 13.4 to about 5.5.
User visually confirmed all joints looked normal.
Small finishing move did not further approach original clearance targets.
Do not keep forcing the original shoulder_front/elbow clearance angles; recapture the current stable posture as a safer table clearance if visually acceptable.
Parallel shoulder_front plus elbow removed the shoulder-front-first path issue but still settled at the same stable posture.
This points to insufficient clearance-specific gains/torque for the final few degrees, or an over-aggressive original clearance target.
Watch shoulder_side and shoulder_front torque before increasing to 20 degrees.
20 degree full-arm synchronous nudge is stable only with nudge auto-gains and long 24 second duration.
Shoulder_side and shoulder_front torque are relatively high; do not increase beyond 20 degrees as a default full-arm synchronous test.
The earlier 20 degree uniform-gain test failed with severe shaking.

full_arm_7joints_no_claw_20deg_sync_nudg.lesson: Do not run all 7 joints as a synchronous 20 degree nudge. Recover to home, then test large moves by staged joint groups or lower gains.

elbow,wrist_side,wrist_home_elbow_first.lesson: Do not home this combination elbow-first. Recover wrist and wrist_side first, then elbow.

elbow,wrist_side,wrist_home_wrist_first_.lesson: Single-command home with wrist,wrist_side,elbow reduced shaking versus elbow-first, but still shook. Do not use as a verified recovery strategy yet.
Use --auto-gains for mixed wrist and elbow home. Unified high kp caused shaking; per-joint gains removed it.

elbow,wrist_side,wrist_recover_wrist_fir.lesson: For elbow plus wrist recovery, home wrist and wrist_side first, then home elbow separately.
